feature: Shift-click and command-click pick several rows in the Layers and Measurements lists
summary: Several layers or measurements can now be selected from the list the way the Finder does it: shift-click for a run of rows, command-click to add or drop one. Until now the only way to select more than one was a marquee on the canvas.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. next-measure-panel is on by default. Open a screenshot and draw four or five measurements with the Measure tool (I).

try.do: In the Measurements list click the first row, then shift-click the third row. Three rows highlight, the three calipers get outlines on the canvas, and the list ends with a line reading 3 measurements selected.
Open the Measure menu. It reads Copy Measurements; choose it and paste into a text editor. You get exactly those three lines, in list order.
Command-click the second row. It leaves the selection and the count line drops to 2. Command-click it again and it is back.
Shift-click a row further down. The run grows from the first row you clicked; anything you added with command-click stays in.
Click a row on the canvas, then shift-click a row in the list. The run starts from the layer you clicked on the canvas.
In the Layers list, shift-click two annotation rows, then click the eye on one of them. All of the selected rows hide together, in one undo step.
Command-click a layer's thumbnail (the small picture, not its name). The layer's pixels load as a selection, the same as before.

evaluate: Did your hand reach for shift-click before reading any of this, and did it do what you expected on the first try?
Does the count line under the list earn its space, or would you rather the inspector said something richer about the selection?
Command-click on the thumbnail still means Select Pixels while command-click on the name means toggle. Is that split obvious, or does it bite?
After a shift-click, is it clear which row the next shift-click will range from?
Should shift-clicking across a hidden or locked row include it in the selection, as it does now?
rough: The Layers menu items Duplicate Layer, Delete Layer and the four arrange commands stay disabled under a multi-selection, list or marquee alike. The Delete key on the canvas and the row context menu's Delete still remove the whole selection. Filed as a follow-up.
The inspector shows no properties for a multi-selection; the count line under the list is the only acknowledgement. Batch editing of shared properties is out of scope here.

Verified by tests, a build and a probe launch only. The loop cannot send real modifier-clicks on this machine, and synthetic events reach the tap gesture for command-click but not for plain or shift clicks, so shift-click on a live row was not exercised by hand.
